prompt: Average monthly temperature in a city is modelled by $T(x) = 4\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{6}\right) + 7$, where $x$ is the number of months since January. What is the period of this model, in months?
hint: Period $= \frac{2\pi}{B}$, where $B$ is whatever multiplies $x$ inside the cosine.

hints.text: Period $= \frac{2\pi}{B}$, where $B$ is whatever multiplies $x$ inside the cosine.

explanation: The coefficient of $x$ inside the cosine is $B = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
A period of $12$ months is exactly what you want for a model of the seasons — it repeats once a year.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check with the calendar
steps: At $x = 12$ (the next January) it gives $4\cos(2\pi) + 7 = 11$ degrees again.
The model has come full circle after $12$ months, so the period is $12$.
